newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end down, despite short-covering.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end down, despite short-covering.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished the day lower, despite a steady stream of short-covering after last week's sharp selloff, traders and analysts said.
They said both June T-bonds and Eurodollar futures were too oversold technically to garner much selling interest.
Attempts to push the market lower only backfired, as evidenced by June bonds' ability to trade near the upper end of the daily trading range at the end of the day, they said.
In fact June bonds hit 110-07/32, a session high, after one French-based firm sold a large amount at 109-28/32 to 110-00 without triggering a rush of sellers in the pit.
The firm sold about 5,000 June T-bonds throughout the day.

June T-bonds held losses at 109-24/32, above key support levels at 109-21/32, the low from January 30; 109-20/32, a 200-day moving average; and 109-19/32, a 62 percent retracement level from the contract's 5-1/2-month upmove.

Some traders were impressed with June's ability to hold above these levels after the U.S. February National Association of Purchasing Management index rose more than average trade expectations. NAPM rose to 53.1, versus estimates of 52.9 against January's 52.0.

"What we're seeing right now is a fairly solid economy, one that our members are optimistic about," Norbert Ore, chairman of the NAPM business survey committee, said in a teleconference after the index was released at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
On Tuesday, weekly chain store sales data, January leading economic indicators and January new home sales will be released.
Most traders are looking for continued choppy range trade ahead of the second leg of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were off 09/32 at 110-05/32, 10-year notes were off 03/32 at 107-19/32, munibonds were down 07/32 at 114-00, June T-bills were off 0.025 at 94.745, and June Eurodollars were down 0.025 at 94.185. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
